resources.string: Advanced features are unlocked. This reveals the dashboard menu\'s \"Live Bitcoin\" link; more may move here in future versions (secure pages, power tools).
Enter your unlock code to reveal advanced features (currently the dashboard menu\'s \"Live Bitcoin\" link).
Offline, temperature, fan, reject-rate and restart alerts with recovery notices.
Add remote LANs reachable through your Tailscale subnet router, e.g. 192.168.50.0/24. They appear as quick-fill options on the Add screen.
Accent color used across the app. Status colors (online/offline) don\'t change.
Show estimated revenue, power cost, and energy use on the dashboard.
Show block-finding probability on the dashboard.
Arrange the dashboard\'s blocks — e.g. move Pool and MMP below the miner list. Cards still only appear when their feature is on.
Which make-tag button the Fleet table shows for labelling miners.
Show the \"Exit Hi3 Hashkit?\" confirmation when tapping the exit button.
Pin the dashboard to one farm: the farm selector row disappears and only that farm\'s miners show — tighter layout when you run one site.
Read-only fleet summary and per-site rollups from your Mining Management Platform.
API key (saved — enter to replace, blank to clear)
API key (mint one in the MMP admin UI)

What is transmitted while enabled: your MMP API key in the request header, over HTTPS to the MMP URL above, about once a minute while the app is open — read-only fleet queries, nothing uploaded. The key is stored encrypted with the Android Keystore. Off by default.
Run a local, read-only web server: an HTML fleet dashboard any browser or TV on the LAN can open, plus a Prometheus /metrics endpoint for Grafana. No auth — for a private LAN/tailnet only.
While the app is open: dashboard at http://<this-device-ip>:%1$d/ and metrics at /metrics. Read-only (GET only); exposes totals + per-miner data, no controls.
Poll every ~15 min while the app is closed (Android may delay this; it is not continuous real-time monitoring).
Each farm refreshes at its own interval while you\'re viewing it; the default applies when no farm is active.
Opt-in: checks AxeOS (Bitaxe) releases on GitHub and flags miners that are behind. No flashing from the app; nothing is contacted while off.
When a miner stays offline past the threshold, power-cycle its smart plug (if set) or reboot it — once, with a cooldown. Every attempt is audited.
Runs the smart-plug over-temp cutoff in the background (with a persistent notification) even when the app is closed, and re-arms after a reboot. Only useful if you\'ve set a plug cutoff on a miner.
Send fleet + per-miner telemetry to a local MQTT broker (e.g. the Mosquitto add-on in Home Assistant). Opt-in; totals and per-miner hashrate/power/temp only — no addresses or credentials.
Password (saved — enter to replace, blank to clear)
Publish MQTT-discovery config so miners appear as HA devices/entities automatically.
Published while the app is open, each poll. The password is stored encrypted in the Android Keystore. Point Prometheus/HA at this broker.
Read-only pool-side view of your workers, correlated with local miner readings on the dashboard.
%1$s support is on the way. Its API needs verifying before we send anything, so this pool contacts nothing yet — pick another pool to load live stats.

What is transmitted while enabled: your %1$s (and token if set), inside an HTTPS request to %2$s, about once a minute while the app is open. Nothing else — no miner telemetry, no local IPs, no worker passwords. Off by default; turning it off stops all pool requests immediately.
Mirror alerts to your own push service so they reach you when the app is closed — no cloud account of ours. Fires only for active alerts.
Suppress alert notifications during a nightly window. Alerts are still recorded and appear in the daily digest.
One summary notification per day of the last 24h of alerts.
Require fingerprint/face or your device PIN to open the app (relocks after 1 minute in the background).
Unavailable: set up a screen lock (PIN/biometric) on this device first.
Protects the app UI. Note: exported backups and the on-disk database are protected by Android\'s standard app sandboxing, not by this lock.
The app\'s only external request; a single HTTPS GET carrying no miner data. Off by default — see docs/SECURITY.md.
Opt-in: a single HTTPS GET (no miner data) so the dashboard can estimate revenue and profit. Off by default; enter a price manually instead if you prefer.

Checks the official GitHub release and installs the signed update over the top — your miners, telemetry history, logs and settings are all kept. Android may ask you to allow installing updates from this app.
Waiting for Android\'s confirmation — tap Update in the system dialog.
Installing… the app will restart when done.
Allow \"Install unknown apps\" for Hashkit in the settings screen that just opened, then come back and tap again.
Full backup (miners, farms, pools, rules, settings…)
Auto-backup weekly: on (tap to change folder)
Last auto-backup: %1$s — keeps the newest 8, plaintext JSON.

Backups contain miner addresses and worker names. Encrypt with a passphrase (AES-256) to share or store safely; a plaintext backup is for your own device only. CSV and diagnostics redact wallets; diagnostics also redact IP addresses.
Enter a passphrase to encrypt the backup (AES-256), or leave blank for a plaintext JSON backup.
Could not read the selected file.
Adds clearly-labeled synthetic miners; they never mix with real totals when off.
That QR isn\'t a bare payout address (looks like a bitcoin: URI). Scan the plain address.
Kasa KP125M / EP25 and Tapo plugs need your TP-Link account for their local login (older Kasa like the KP115 do not). Used only on your LAN; nothing is sent to TP-Link.
TP-Link password (saved — enter to replace, blank to clear)
The password is stored encrypted with the Android Keystore and used only to open an encrypted session with plugs on your local network.
